Verdict

No confirmed signs of a malicious supply-chain compromise were identified. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • In the provided text corpus, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, setup.py install-time execution, clearly malicious PEP 517 build hooks, or malicious import-time side effects.
  • CLI commands and subprocess.run() usage in elhaz/cli/__main__.py appear to require user invocation of elhaz exec or elhaz shell; they are normal CLI behavior, not install-time or interpreter-start automatic execution.
  • Daemon-related behavior also appears to be a documented, user-controlled CLI feature, with no evidence of automatic persistence installation.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • **Credential harvesting:** The package is explicitly an AWS temporary credential broker, and the docs/code reference AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN. However, the provided evidence does not show broad environment/home-directory/SSH key/CI token harvesting, stealthy collection, or coupling with external exfiltration.
  • **Archive staging / exfiltration:** No evidence was found of archiving or staging credentials/files, or uploading them to a webhook, C2, raw IP, or drop service. The raw.githubusercontent.com references in README/PKG-INFO appear to be documentation/image references.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence was found of systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, shell profile modification, startup folder registration, or self-reinstallation.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence was found of Kubernetes service-account token access, Docker socket use, cloud metadata abuse, CI publish-token theft, or GitHub Actions workflow injection.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** No evidence was found of eval/exec, base64/zlib/marshal loaders, obfuscated downloaders, or platform-specific staged payload selection.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The sdist contains .github/, .gitignore, and documentation image files, but the provided evidence does not support treating them as hidden payloads or malicious distribution-integrity anomalies.
  • docs/_static/*.png and favicon.ico appear to be documentation static assets, not unexplained native binaries.
  • The dependencies listed in PKG-INFO are consistent with the package’s stated AWS credential-broker purpose. No evidence was provided of sudden malicious dependency insertion, typosquatting, or wheel/sdist mismatch.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The input corpus does not include the full pyproject.toml and all source files, so complete verification of build backend, entry points, and packaging configuration is limited.
  • The reviewed artifact is the elhaz-0.5.2.tar.gz sdist. If a wheel exists for the same version, it should be compared against the sdist for file or behavior mismatches.
  • Binary static documentation assets were not decoded or analyzed for steganography/hidden payloads based on the provided text-only corpus.
